newsitem.title: USA: Ex-Clinton adviser in sex scandal now faces divorce.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Clinton adviser in sex scandal now faces divorce.

text.p: Dick Morris, President Bill Clinton's former top political adviser who quit after a sex scandal in the midst of the 1996 campaign, now faces the end of his marriage, the Daily News reported on Sunday.
Attorney Eileen McGann, married to Morris for 20 years, told the tabloid that she made up her mind to end the marriage when she was in California last week.

"It had been one crisis after another and I finally had a chance to think," she told the News. "I had really hoped and believed that as time went by this would disappear as a public issue and become a private issue between Dick and me, but that didn't turn out to be true. I realised it would never go away."

Morris, in a statement issued by his publisher Random House, said: "I'm devastated and deeply upset. More than anything else, I wanted to stay married to Eileen and I feel sadder than I can say that my own conduct made that impossible."

McGann said her world became upended after a supermarket tabloid reported last August that her husband had an affair with a $200-an-hour call girl, Sherry Rowlands, who boasted that Morris let her listen to phone calls with Clinton.
McGann, 48, said she felt she had lost her privacy completely when a second scandal broke and she learned that her husband had a daughter by a woman in Texas.
Morris, 48, resigned as a Clinton campaign strategist after reports of his affair with the hooker surfaced during the Democratic National Convention in August 1996.
He signed a book deal with Random House shortly after resigning his post. His 350-page book, "Behind the Oval Office: Winning the Presidency in the Nineties," will be released on Jan. 15.
